title: Man shot by police in west Hamilton has died
subtitle: In a news release Sunday evening, the SIU said based on its investigation, it does not appear the man discharged a firearm.
article: This story was updated from an earlier version with inaccurate information from the SIU.
A 43-year-old man shot during an interaction with Hamilton police Saturday evening has died, the province's Special Investigations Unit has confirmed.
In a news release Sunday evening, the SIU said based on its investigation, it does not appear the man discharged a firearm.
Hamilton police responded to the fifth floor of a west Hamilton condominium building around 5 p.m. on Saturday for a report of a man acting in a threatening manner.

The SIU said officers became involved in an interaction with a person of interest. Two officers discharged their firearms and the man was struck. He was sent to hospital where he was pronounced dead at 12:47 a.m. on Sunday.
An autopsy is scheduled for Monday morning in Toronto.
A Hamilton police officer was sent to hospital with minor injuries and released.
In an earlier news release, the SIU said a police officer and a man in his 30s were injured in an exchange of gunfire.
The SIU has designated two subjects of the investigation and two witness officers.

On Saturday evening, Hamilton police spokesperson Jackie Penman told the Spectator the officer was injured after responding to a 911 call at 1964 Main St. W. , a condominium building in the Ainslie Wood West neighbourhood.
"Our officer responded to a 911 call and they were confronted by a male with a firearm," said Penman.
The SIU is an independent agency that probes circumstances involving police and civilians that result in serious injury, death or allegations of sexual assault.

Photos from the scene Saturday night - a three tower apartment building complex on the westernmost edge of the old city of Hamilton - showed an area cordoned off by police tape and several armed officers on scene.
Anyone with information that could assist the investigation - including video or photos - is asked to contact the SIU's lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529 or contact the agency online .
